title.narrative: Urgent Support for war-affected people through providing them with food assistance and implementing small garden initiatives

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtIn response to the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip, the project “Urgent Support for War-Affected People Through Providing Them with Food Assistance and Implementing Small Garden Initiatives” provides an immediate, lifesaving and recovery-oriented response. It aims to address acute food insecurity among displaced and conflict-affected families by delivering in-kind food assistance, establishing small household gardens, and supporting open-land (OL) farmers through conditional cash assistance. The intervention seeks not only to meet urgent food needs but also to restore small-scale agricultural activities and strengthen local food production during the ceasefire period.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will target 2,080 households, reaching 11,648 individuals (5,801 females and 5,847 males), including 2,959 women, 2,737 girls, 3,087 men, and 2,865 boys. Beneficiaries are residing in informal shelters, displacement camps, damaged homes, and heavily affected neighborhoods in Gaza City, North Gaza, and Deir Al Balah. These families represent some of the most vulnerable populations, many facing catastrophic levels of food insecurity.ltbrgtImplemented over six months under the oPt HF 2025 Third Reserve Allocation – Track 2: 48 Hours Envelope, the project directly contributes to the Food Security Cluster objective of improving nutrition outcomes through flexible modalities (in-kind and cash), complemented by small-scale gardening initiatives. It aligns with the Flash Appeal priorities to provide emergency diversified food assistance and restore local food production and agricultural livelihoods.ltbrgt UWAC will ensure coordinated implementation and transparent financial management.ltbrgtThe project includes three main components. First, the distribution of 6,000 food parcels (2,000 dry and 4,000 fresh) to 2,000 households over three rounds, with each household receiving two rounds of fresh parcels and one round of dry parcels. This intervention will enhance dietary diversity and reduce immediate food gaps among highly vulnerable families.ltbrgtSecond, 40 vulnerable households will receive agricultural inputs and technical support to establish home gardens, promoting self-sufficiency, resilience, and improved access to fresh vegetables, with particular attention to female-headed households.ltbrgtThird, 40 OL farmers will receive conditional cash assistance to rehabilitate and cultivate 80 dunums of accessible land. This support will help revive local food production, mitigate rising food prices, and partially compensate for the extensive destruction of Gaza’s agricultural lands.ltbrgtThrough this integrated approach, the project combines emergency relief with early recovery efforts, strengthening food security, restoring livelihoods, and rebuilding resilience among war-affected communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
